Title: On linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes have been proposed for new applications as countermeasures against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault injection attacks (FIA) in the context of direct sum masking (DSM). The countermeasure against FIA may lead to a vulnerability for SCA when the whole algorithm needs to be masked (in environments like smart cards). This led to a variant of the LCD and LCP problems, where several results have been obtained intensively for LCD codes, but only partial results have been derived for LCP codes. Given the gap between the thin results and their particular importance, this paper aims to reduce this by further studying the LCP of codes in special code families and, precisely, the characterisation and construction mechanism of LCP codes of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields. Notably, we propose constructing explicit LCP of codes from elliptic curves. Besides, we also study the security parameters of the derived LCP of codes $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D})$ (notably for cyclic codes), which are given by the minimum distances $d(\mathcal{C})$ and $d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)$. Further, we show that for LCP algebraic geometry codes $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$, the dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{D}$ under some specific conditions we exhibit. Finally, we investigate whether MDS LCP of algebraic geometry codes exist (MDS codes are among the most important in coding theory due to their theoretical significance and practical interests). Construction schemes for obtaining LCD codes from any algebraic curve were given in 2018 by Mesnager, Tang and Qi in [``Complementary dual algebraic geometry codes", IEEE Trans. Inform Theory, vol. 64(4), 2390--3297, 2018]. To our knowledge, it is the first time LCP of algebraic geometry codes has been studied.

gold.abstract: Due to their widespread applications, linear complementary pairs (LCPs) have attracted much attention in recent years. In this paper, we determine explicit construction of non-special divisors of degree $g$ and $g-1$ on Kummer extensions with specific properties. In addition, we present several methods for constructing LCPs of algebraic geometry codes (AG Codes) via Kummer extensions. These results are applied in constructing explicit LCPs of AG Codes from subcovers of the BM curve, elliptic function fields, hyperelliptic function fields and other function fields. It is important to mention that we construct several families LCPs of MDS AG Codes from elliptic function fields and we obtain some linear complementary dual (LCD) codes from certain maximal elliptic function fields and hyperelliptic function fields.

It also gives binary examples with better parameters than known LCD codes and a programming bound for the case \(d(C)=d(D^\perp)\).

The paper’s algebraic equivalence between \(C\) and \(D^\perp\) for constacyclic LCPs creates a structural symmetry that can be exploited as a side-channel leakage model. Specifically, if an implementation uses constacyclic LCPs for masking, the equivalence implies that faulting or probing one component reveals information about the other with the same algebraic action. This causal link allows us to derive information-theoretic leakage bounds from the code parameter \(d(C)\) alone, not from the pair. The mechanism connects code algebra (equivalence under constacyclic shift) to physical security metrics (mutual information between faulted codeword and secret).

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Construct a set of binary constacyclic LCPs with varying \(d(C)\) from [paper-c]’s tables.
- Simulate a masking scheme where a secret \(s\) is encoded as \(c+s\) with \(c \in C\) and \(s \in D\).
- Apply a fault model: an attacker flips up to \(t\) coordinates in the encoded word.
- Measure the mutual information \(I(S; \text{faulted word})\) under the equivalence \(D^\perp \equiv C\).
- Validate against an LCD-based baseline using the programming bound from [paper-c].
- Hypothesis: mutual information collapses to a function of \(d(C)\) for constacyclic LCPs, but not for general LCPs, confirming the algebraic leakage channel.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose using the algebraic equivalence \(D^\perp \equiv C\) for constacyclic LCPs to model side-channel leakage in code-based masking. By simulating fault attacks on encoded secrets, we hypothesize that the mutual information between secret and observation depends only on \(d(C)\), enabling a single-parameter security bound. This connects coding-theoretic structure to physical security metrics, offering a design rule for choosing LCP parameters beyond existing LCD bounds.

FINAL IDEA: The constacyclic LCP equivalence \(D^\perp \equiv C\) enables a fault-leakage model where the mutual information between secret and faulty codeword is governed solely by \(d(C)\), yielding a new single-parameter side-channel security bound.

It also gives binary examples with better parameters than known LCD codes and a programming bound for the case \(d(C)=d(D^\perp)\).

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
The algebraic equivalence \(D^\perp \equiv C\) for constacyclic LCPs creates a structural symmetry that can be causally linked to a fault-leakage channel in code-based masking. If an implementation masks a secret \(s \in D\) by adding \(c \in C\), then a fault that flips coordinates of the encoded word \(c+s\) induces a predictable transformation on the dual code. Because \(D^\perp \equiv C\), the attacker’s observation of the faulty word reveals information about \(s\) through the same algebraic action that relates \(C\) and \(D^\perp\). This operational connection means the mutual information \(I(S; \text{faulted word})\) becomes a function of \(d(C)\) only, not of the pair \((d(C), d(D^\perp))\). The mechanism is causal: the equivalence determines how faults propagate in the dual domain, and the minimum distance \(d(C)\) bounds the number of correctable (non-leaking) fault patterns.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Use the binary constacyclic LCPs from [paper-c]’s tables, selecting instances with varying \(d(C)\) and \(d(D^\perp)=d(C)\).
- Simulate a direct-sum masking scheme: secret \(s\) drawn uniformly from \(D\), mask \(c\) from \(C\), transmitted word \(w = c+s\).
- Fault model: attacker flips up to \(t\) coordinates in \(w\), for \(t = 1, \ldots, d(C)-1\).
- Compute empirical mutual information \(\hat{I}(S; w_{\text{faulty}})\) via Monte Carlo, using the known code structure to compute conditional distributions.
- Validate the single-parameter claim by comparing \(\hat{I}\) across LCPs with same \(d(C)\) but different \(d(D^\perp)\) (using the non-constacyclic examples in [paper-c] where \(d(C)\neq d(D^\perp)\)).
- Hypothesis: for constacyclic LCPs, \(\hat{I}\) collapses to a curve depending only on \(d(C)\); for general LCPs, \(\hat{I}\) depends on both distances, confirming the algebraic leakage channel.
- Use the programming bound from [paper-c] to benchmark leakage versus optimal LCD codes.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose a fault-leakage model for code-based masking that exploits the constacyclic LCP equivalence \(D^\perp \equiv C\). By simulating coordinate faults on masked secrets, we hypothesize that mutual information between secret and faulty observation is governed solely by \(d(C)\), yielding a single-parameter side-channel security bound. The design compares constacyclic and non-constacyclic LCPs to isolate the algebraic effect, providing a coding-theoretic rule for selecting masking codes beyond existing LCD bounds.

FINAL IDEA: The constacyclic LCP equivalence \(D^\perp \equiv C\) implies that fault-induced leakage in direct-sum masking depends only on \(d(C)\), enabling a single-parameter security bound validated by contrasting constacyclic and non-constacyclic code pairs.
